metadata.notes: Path B — Indirect Prompt Injection via Data Sources. Scenario: LegitimateAgentCompromised (Layer 2 AI-Specific). Malicious instructions embedded in documents, emails, or web content the agent is designed to ingest. Agent's data-reading function (first #1) encounters injected instructions, triggering abuse of action capabilities (second #1), leading to unauthorised operations (third #1). Notation: #1→[instant]#1→[instant]#1 + [DRE: C]. Velocity: VC-4 — all three steps execute within the same processing cycle. The critical distinction from Layer 1 attacks: no implementation flaw is involved at any step. Boundary test: if the same file triggered a buffer overflow in the parser → #3 (Exploiting Client). But if the file is parsed correctly and the text contains instructions the agent obeys → #1 (Abuse of Functions). Same file, different generic vulnerability. Source: 'Agentic AI Under the Microscope — Why AI Security Is Not a Threat Category' (Bernhard Kreinz, 2026-02-25).

path_sequence.notes: Agent reads external data source (document, email, web page, API response) containing embedded instructions. Generic vulnerability: designed data ingestion capability — parser works correctly, extracted text contains injected instructions.
Agent follows injected instructions, invoking tool capabilities. Generic vulnerability: instruction-following across entire context window is designed capability.
Unauthorised operations executed via legitimate tool access. Generic vulnerability: scope and trust in agent's authorised tool integrations.
